questions.q: What specific gap does database watcher fill that per-database Azure Monitor dashboards and DMV queries don't?
options: It gives a single, fleet-wide, centralized view across many databases at once, instead of requiring you to check one resource at a time
It replaces the need to ever write T-SQL again
It is the only way to see CPU percentage for a single database
It eliminates the need for Azure Monitor entirely on every workload
questions.explain: Azure Monitor and DMVs are built around one resource at a time; database watcher centralizes monitoring data across an entire registered fleet of databases.

questions.q: What are the three pieces you configure when setting up database watcher?
options: A watcher resource, one or more SQL targets (up to 100 per watcher), and a data store (Azure Data Explorer or Fabric Real-Time Analytics)
A virtual machine, a load balancer, and a firewall rule
A stored procedure, a trigger, and a scheduled job
A Power BI report, a dataset, and a dataflow
questions.explain: The watcher is the resource you create and control, SQL targets are what you register for monitoring, and the data store is where collected data lands.

questions.q: Roughly how many SQL system catalog views and DMVs does database watcher collect data from, per this lesson?
options: More than 70
Exactly 5
Exactly 1,000
It collects no DMV data at all — only Azure Resource Manager metadata
questions.explain: Database watcher transforms data from more than 70 catalog views and DMVs into organized datasets in its data store.

questions.q: What is database watcher's current status, and what does this lesson say you should do before relying on it in production?
options: It is currently in preview; check Microsoft's current documentation for the latest supported regions, limits, and feature state before depending on it in a production runbook
It has been fully general-availability (GA) and unchanged since 2015
It only works with on-premises SQL Server, never Azure SQL
It has been fully deprecated and should never be used
questions.explain: This lesson is explicit that preview features can change and carry different support terms and limitations — worth re-verifying rather than assuming.

questions.q: At the estate-dashboard level, what kind of view does database watcher provide?
options: A heatmap and top-queries ranking across the entire registered fleet, with subscription/resource-group filters
Only a single number showing total storage used across all subscriptions
A list of every stored procedure name in every database, with no other detail
A live video feed of the Azure data center
questions.explain: Estate dashboards (rendered as Azure Workbooks) give a fleet-wide heatmap and a top-queries view across every monitored resource at once.
